title: Who Won the Noughts and Crosses
statement:
Two players, A and B, play noughts and crosses on a 3 × 3 board. A always moves first, then they alternate. moves[i] = [row, col] is the cell taken on turn i, so even turns belong to A and odd turns to B.

A player wins by owning a full row, column or diagonal. The moves are always legal: no cell is taken twice, and the list stops as soon as somebody wins.

Return "A" or "B" if that player has won, "Draw" if the board is full with no winner, and "Pending" if the game is not over yet.

examples.why: A holds (0, 0), (1, 1) and (2, 2): the main diagonal.
B's (1, 1), (0, 2) and (2, 0) form the other diagonal. A has three marks but no line.
Two moves in, nobody has a line and the board still has empty cells.

constraints: All moves are distinct and form a legal game that ends at the first win
hints: The game ends at the first win, so only the player who moved last can have won. Which player is that?
Replay the moves onto a 3 × 3 board and check the 8 lines. Or keep a counter per row, column and diagonal for each player.

With counters: add +1 for A and −1 for B on the move's row, column and, if it lies on one, each diagonal. A counter reaching 3 or −3 means a full line. If nobody wins, it is a draw at 9 moves and pending before that.

explain.intuition:
A board this small can simply be replayed and checked line by line. The interesting part is doing it without the board: a line belongs to one player exactly when all three of its cells are theirs. Give each row, column and diagonal a counter that goes up by 1 for A's marks and down by 1 for B's. A line is A's when its counter hits 3 and B's when it hits −3, because a single opposing mark makes reaching ±3 impossible.

The same counter idea scales to an n × n board with O(n) memory and O(1) work per move, which is why interviewers like it.
steps: For move i at (r, c): let s = +1 if i is even (A), else −1.
Add s to rows[r] and cols[c]; to diag if r === c; to anti if r + c === 2.
If any of those reaches ±3, return the mover.
After all moves, return "Draw" if there were 9, else "Pending".
pitfalls: Returning "Draw" when the board is not full. Fewer than 9 moves without a winner is "Pending".
Returning "Draw" for a full board without checking the last move. A can complete a line on move 9.
Forgetting that the centre cell lies on both diagonals.

solutions.title: Replay on a board
solutions.idea: Mark every move on a 3 × 3 grid, then test all 8 lines for three equal marks.

solutions.title: Signed line counters
solutions.idea: +1 for A and −1 for B on each row, column and diagonal the move touches. A counter at ±3 is a full line.

followups: Generalise to an n × n board where k in a row wins. Do the counters still work?
Given a final board instead of the move list, decide whether it could come from a legal game.
